top_categories.workout_context: 126ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At West Coast Gravel, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
West Coast Gravel's Siuslaw National Forest backroads, Coastal forest gravel forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 53 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of West Coast Gravel. Train it until it feels boring.
6,690ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Race-pace efforts that mimic West Coast Gravel's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At West Coast Gravel, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Low-cadence force work for 6,690ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Smooth pedaling at 53 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.
6,690ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
53 miles on steep Oregon coast forest gravel burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for West Coast Gravel’s 53 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at West Coast Gravel requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on steep oregon coast forest gravel to build confidence. Expect: siuslaw national forest backroads, coastal forest gravel, paved rollout and timed finish.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Over Under, and Gravel Specific to prepare you for 53 miles of steep oregon coast forest gravel in Yachats, Oregon.
